answer.diagnosis: The weights point to a corner-patch shortcut in the top-left of the image, at rows 1-3 and columns 1-3. Many layer-1 units carry large, sign-consistent weights on exactly this 3x3 patch, far larger than the noise-level weights at nearby background pixels. Units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 28 have weights of about +45 to +93 there; these are the units with centre-blob (size) detectors. Units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26 and 29 have weights of about -45 to -99 there; these are the ring/background units. Unit 31 shows a weaker negative version (about -16 to -48). This patch is far from where the blob sits, so it cannot measure blob size. The consistent signs suggest a bright marker in that corner was correlated with one of the classes during training, and the network learned to detect it. I did not trace the patch through layers 2 and 3, so the weights alone do not tell me which class the marker pushes toward. The fix is to zero every layer-1 weight on that 3x3 patch. This leaves the centre and ring weights that respond to blob size untouched.

edits.reason: remove top-left corner marker detector weights
